definitions.explanation: An informal, familiar term for one's wife or someone else's wife. Primarily used by men in casual conversation.

examples.japanese: かみさん⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}いて→聞く：00483_kiku⟧みる⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
かみさん⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手料理|てりょうり}→手料理：12760_teryouri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧⟦うまい→うまい：01279_umai⟧。
examples.english: My wife's home cooking is the best.

examples.japanese: うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧かみさん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{怒|おこ}る→怒る：00876_okoru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{怖|こわ}い→怖い：00864_kowai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{早|はや}く→早い：00514_hayai⟧⟦{帰|かえ}らない→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧。
examples.english: My wife is scary when she's angry, so I'd better get home early.

notes:
USAGE:
Used mainly by middle-aged and older men to refer to their own wife in casual settings. It has a down-to-earth, familiar tone. Not appropriate in formal situations, where ⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧ or ⟦{家内|かない}→家内：00958_kanai⟧ would be used instead.

The word comes from {上|かみ}さん, originally a respectful term for a woman of higher status or the lady of the house.

REGISTER:
Informal and spoken. Common among working-class and older male speakers. Younger men tend to prefer ⟦{奥|おく}さん→奥さん：02853_okusan⟧ (for others' wives) or ⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧ (for their own).
